subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Skimming, True/False/Not Given and vocabulary development
outcomes: Skim a text and choose the best title with reasons
Decide if statements are True, False or Not Given and correct false ones
Match new words and phrases from the text with their meanings

tf.s: Skimming means reading quickly to get the general idea of a text.
tf.why: You skim for the main idea, not for details.

tf.s: A title that is too general is the best choice for a text.
tf.why: The best title fits the whole text closely, not too generally.

tf.s: A title that describes only one section of the text is not the best title.
tf.why: The best title must cover the whole text.

tf.s: 'Not Given' means the text does not give that information.
tf.why: You cannot find it as true or false in the text.

tf.s: 'Not Given' means the statement is the opposite of the text.
tf.why: That would be 'False'; 'Not Given' means the information is missing.

tf.s: The Virgin Atlantic plane was entirely powered by biofuel.
tf.why: It was only partly powered by biofuel.

tf.s: In T/F/NG tasks, small words like 'partly' and 'entirely' can change the answer.
tf.why: Adverbs and qualifying words change the meaning.

tf.s: The KLM flight in the text carried 171 passengers.
tf.why: The corrected statement gives 171 passengers on the KLM flight.

tf.s: When a statement is False, you do not need to correct it.
tf.why: The task asks you to correct false statements.

tf.s: You must read every word slowly to skim a text.
tf.why: Skimming is quick reading for the general idea.

o: Reading quickly for the main idea

boxes.why: Title c covers the whole text.

boxes.why: They did not fit the text closely enough.
A good title covers the whole text.

boxes.q: How was the Virgin Atlantic plane powered?
boxes.why: The plane was only partly powered by biofuel.

o: The text has no information on it
boxes.why: The answer is not in the text.

boxes.q: What should you note carefully in T/F/NG?
What must you do with a False statement?
boxes.why: Correcting shows you understood the text.

hunt.q: Reading fast for the main idea
Problem with titles a and b
Answer if the text has no info

mcq.q: What should you note carefully in True/False/Not Given tasks?
o: Adverbs and qualifying words, like 'partly' and 'entirely'
mcq.why: Small words can change whether a statement is true.

mcq.q: What is the difference between 'False' and 'Not Given'?
o: False: the text says the opposite; Not Given: the text has no information
False: the text agrees; Not Given: the text disagrees
Not Given means the statement is true
mcq.why: Check whether the text contradicts the statement or says nothing.

o: Getting the general idea, for example to choose a title
mcq.why: Skimming helps you understand what the whole text is about.

mcq.q: Which airlines are mentioned in the text?
mcq.why: The text talks about Virgin Atlantic and KLM biofuel flights.

mcq.q: Statement: 'The Virgin Atlantic plane was entirely powered by biofuel.' What is the answer and correction?
o: False: it was partly powered by biofuel
Not Given: the text says nothing

mcq.q: A statement mentions the colour of the KLM plane, but the text says nothing about colour. What is the answer?
mcq.why: If the text has no information, the answer is Not Given.

mcq.q: You have one minute to choose a title for a long text. What should you do?
o: Skim the text for the main idea
Look up every word in a dictionary
mcq.why: Skimming quickly shows the overall topic.

mcq.q: One title is too general, one covers only one section, and one covers the whole text. Which should you choose?
o: The title that covers the whole text
mcq.why: The best title matches the whole text, like title c.

mcq.q: Why is title d not the best choice?
o: It refers to only one section of the text
mcq.why: The best title must describe the whole text.

mcq.q: Why do adverbs like 'partly' matter in a T/F/NG task?
o: One adverb can make a statement false even if the rest is correct
Adverbs always make a statement true
They only matter in spelling tests
mcq.why: Reading carefully stops you from choosing the wrong answer.
